reason: The 10:50 firing found a successor recorded and assumed-alive, but list_sessions showed it REQUIRES_ACTION since 10:55, waiting on a permission prompt for update_trigger. A child waiting for approval waits forever — the owner may never read it — so that is a permanent stop, which A10 forbids. 'A successor exists' was not the same question as 'the chain is moving'.
what_changed_one_thing: The eta-loop trigger prompt. The parent session is now a spawner, not a worker, and the firing has a third branch for stalled-but-present. This was authored by the blocked child; it was right, and it was the very change the approval prompt was blocking. Applying it from the parent, which already holds that permission, is the fix and the demonstration at once.

the_thing_worth_reading_twice: REQUIRES_ACTION reads as alive in every summary field and is not. The previous handoff recorded a successor and said the chain was live; both were true and the chain was still stopped. Presence is not motion. The trigger prompt now says to look at the successor's actual status rather than at whether one was recorded.
known_gaps: Detection of a stalled child is indirect: eta-loop's liveness points at this file, so a chain that stops recording shows up as overdue after its 60m cadence. Nothing reads session status on a schedule, so up to an hour can pass before a blocked child is visible. That is a real hole, not a covered case.
The child prompt now forbids approval-requiring operations, but nothing enforces it. If a future child tries one anyway it blocks again, and only the hourly parent firing will notice.
